messages:
kevin: FYI customer ACME reports p99 spikes from ~120ms -> 900ms over last 2 hours, started after last night's kernel tweak. https://dash.redwood/acme/latency :grimacing:

maria: Looking. Which kernel path changed? flashopt or sdpa?

kevin: We flipped a compile flag for flash path: `FLASH_OPT_LEVEL=3` + `-DFAST_KV` in the nightly build. infra-bot deploy shows rollout to canary pool at 02:12 UTC.

aj: I see a wave of SDPA->flash fallback in the logs around 02:25. Samples: `kernel_select: preferred=sdpa, attempted=flashattn_v2, fallback=flashattn_v1`, then `kv_cache_miss` spikes.

sasha: @aj could this be the kernel priority heuristics mis-evaluating long prefix distribution? We recently tightened hysteresis for flashopt.

aj: Possible. Repro steps I used locally:
```
# repro script
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"'"-repeat-512-"'"}'
```
This produces ~p99 700ms on canary.

julia: Can we temporarily route ACME to `attn_variant=sdpa_stable`? We can apply per-customer kernel override in routing rules.

kevin: Yes please. ACME is on hosted tier, low risk. Requesting immediate override.

maria: I'll push the routing rule: `POST /v1/admin/routing/overrides {"customer":"acme","attn_variant":"sdpa_stable","until":"2026-03-18T05:00:00Z"}`. Applying now. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: override applied to 12 nodes in us-west-2; config ver=2026-03-17_0308.

kevin: After override p95 ~120ms, p99 down to ~220ms. Good short-term win. Still need root cause and fix.

aj: Next steps: 1) roll back the `FLASH_OPT_LEVEL=3` compile flag on next build and re-run canary; 2) add extra telemetry on kv_cache_hit_ratio and kernel_select_reason; 3) run microbench of long-prefix sequences for flashattn_v2.

sasha: I'll run model-synthetic evals against the nightly build and compare token-level timings across kernels.

maria: Also create an incident ticket and note customer impact + mitigation. Kevin, update ACME CS that we applied a targeted routing override and are working on a permanent fix.

kevin: On it. I'll send a note: "We've applied a temporary kernel override to reduce latency while we investigate. No data loss. Expect follow-up by EOD."

aj: If rollback shows improvement, we can stage a hotfix build without the aggressive flashopt flags and FBW to prod in 4 hours. Otherwise enable additional KV prefetch heuristics as fallback.

julia: Can we add a test in CI that runs a tiny long-prefix load profile to catch this class of regressions?

sasha: Good idea — adding a short gating job that runs the curl repro above with 200 requests and asserts p99 < 400ms for canary.

maria: Summary of milestones: (1) ACME override applied, (2) rollback candidate queued, (3) synthetic evals running, (4) CI gating job PR opened. Keep thread updated. :spiral_note_pad:

kevin: Thanks. I'll close the support escalation once CS confirms the message went out. Ping if p99 creeps back up.

support-bot: Support ticket #SUP-1138 updated: mitigation applied, customer notified.

aj: tagging this for follow-up: add link to repro artifacts and kernel trace logs in the ticket. I'll attach when done.

maria: Nice work team. Quick wins + durable fix plan looks good. :thumbsup:
